questions.knowledge_point: Negating a Predicate Expressed in Plain English
questions.problem:
$\,$ $5$ divides $x.$

The predicate $P(x)$ is given above. Which of following represents $¬P(x)?$
questions.worked_solution:
The symbol "$¬$" represents negation. So, our task is to negate the given sentence. 

To negate our plain English sentence, we place the words "It is not true that" in front of it. This gives the following:

$\,$ It is not true that $5$ divides $x.$

In other words, $5$ does *not* divide $x.$ Therefore, $¬P(x)$ means the following:

$\,$ $5$ does **not** divide $x.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Truth Set of Predicate's Negation
questions.problem:
Find the truth set of $¬P(x)$ given the following predicate defined over the universal set $R:$

$\,$ $P(x):$ $1-x\ge 5$
questions.worked_solution:
The truth set of $¬P(x)$ is the *complement* of the truth set of $P(x):$

$$
{T}_{¬P}={\overset{―}{T}}_{P}
$$

To find the the truth set of $P(x),$ we solve the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}1-x & \ge 5 \\ -x & \ge 4 \\ x & \le -4\end{aligned}
$$

So, the truth set of $P(x)$ is
${T}_{P}=(-\infty ,-4].$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}_{¬P} & ={\overset{―}{T}}_{P} \\  & =\overset{―}{(-\infty ,-4]} \\  & =(-4,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the truth set of $¬P(x)$ given the following predicate defined over the universal set of integers between $-3$ and $3,$ inclusive: 

$\,$ $P(x):$ ${x}^{2}=4$
questions.worked_solution:
The truth set of $¬P(x)$ is the *complement* of the truth set of $P(x):$

$$
{T}_{¬P}={\overset{―}{T}}_{P},
$$

The truth set of $P(x)$ is the set of integers between $-3$ and $3,$ inclusive, whose square is $4,$ i.e.,

$$
{T}_{P}={-2,2}.
$$

 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}_{¬P} & ={\overset{―}{T}}_{P} \\  & =\overset{―}{{-2,2}} \\  & ={-3,-1,0,1,3}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
$\qquad$ $x \nleq \sqrt{2}$

The predicate $P(x)$ is given above. Write down $\neg P(x).$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
In plain English, our predicate $P(x)$ means the following:

$\qquad$ $x$ is not smaller than or equal to $\sqrt{2}.$

The symbol "$\neg$" represents negation. To negate our plain English expression, we place the words "It is not true that" in front of it. This gives the following:

$\qquad$ It is not true that $x$ is not smaller than or equal to $\sqrt{2}.$

In other words, $x$ *is* *smaller than or equal to* $\sqrt{2}.$ Therefore, $\neg P(x)$ means the following:

$\qquad$ $x\leq \sqrt{2}$
